# Copy-ready WebApp GitHub Actions standard and setup docs

## Outcome

New and existing django-mojo WebApps get a copy-ready GitHub Actions workflow and operator/developer documentation for merge-to-deploy using the canonical action and `MOJO_DEPLOY_KEY`.

## Why

The skeleton should make the standard obvious without activating deployment in the skeleton repository itself or confusing WebApp releases with the existing backend/API webhook flow.

## Spec

### Acceptance criteria

- An inactive example caller workflow lives under `examples/github/workflows/` and triggers on push to a configurable deployment branch plus `workflow_dispatch`.
- The example builds the app, then passes `MOJO_DEPLOY_KEY` only to the deploy step.
- It uses `contents: read`, non-cancelling per-WebApp concurrency, Git SHA versions, and repository variables for API URL and WebApp ID.
- Setup docs explain that an admin creates/links one service key per WebApp, stores it as the GitHub Actions secret named exactly `MOJO_DEPLOY_KEY`, and developers receive no deploy key.
- Docs cover branch protection, rotation, monorepo GitHub Environments, manual hold opt-out, deployment failure/rollback behavior, and action version pinning.
- Existing CI/CD docs clearly distinguish backend/API webhook deployment from WebApp GitHub Actions deployment.
- The example and docs pass repository documentation/static checks.

### Investigation notes

- Keep the workflow under examples so django-mojo-skeleton itself does not deploy.
- Copy or generate the example during project creation only if an established skeleton mechanism already supports that safely.

### Constraints

- Preserve the exact secret name `MOJO_DEPLOY_KEY`.
- Do not check in credentials or require developers to install credentials locally.
- Do not add an active workflow to the skeleton repository root.

### Likely files

- `examples/github/workflows/deploy-webapp.yml`
- `docs/django_developer/deployment/ci-cd.md`
- related WebApp deployment/setup docs and README links

### Out of scope

- Creating credentials in a live MojoVerify WebApp.
- Modifying the reusable action implementation.
- Changing backend/API webhook semantics.

## Plan

1. Add an inactive example caller at `examples/github/workflows/deploy-webapp.yml`: push to main and manual dispatch, read-only contents permission, non-cancelling per-WebApp concurrency, ordinary project build steps, then the central action using Git SHA.
2. Pass `MOJO_DEPLOY_KEY` only on the deploy step; source API URL and WebApp ID from repository variables.
3. Rewrite CI/CD guidance to distinguish backend/API GitHub webhook deployment from static WebApp GitHub Actions release deployment.
4. Add a setup runbook for the one-time admin `link_key` operation, `gh secret set MOJO_DEPLOY_KEY`, branch protection, rotation, monorepo environments, manual-hold opt-out, rollback behavior, and action pinning.
5. Link the example from the deployment index and verify YAML/docs/static checks.
